title: Reading simple sentences
examples: Teacher, how do I know when to stop reading?
Can you show me how to point when I read?
What does it mean to read for sense?

explain.say: Today we are learning to read simple sentences aloud. We will use our fingers to help us read.
Use your finger to point under each word as you read it. This helps your eyes follow along correctly. Look at this sentence. Touch each word with your finger.

draw.text: The cat sat on the mat.

explain.say: Remember that every sentence starts with a big letter. This letter is called a capital letter. We must say it clearly at the start. Look at the word 'The'. It starts with a capital 'T'.
When you finish reading, you must say the full stop sound. This means your voice goes quiet and stops. It tells us the sentence is finished. Say 'The dog sat.' and then make a little stop sound.

draw.text: Full stop means stopping your voice.

explain.say: After reading, we must check if it makes sense. Read it once, then read it again to make sure it sounds right. This is reading for sense. Does 'The dog ate the car' make sense? No, it does not.

faq.q: Why do I have to point with my finger?
faq.a: Pointing helps your eyes stay focused on the right words. It keeps your reading steady and accurate. You can also point with your finger when you read.
asks: How do I keep my eyes on the words?
Should I point when I read?

faq.q: What is the difference between a capital letter and a small letter?
faq.a: A capital letter is a big letter used at the start of a sentence. A small letter is the regular letter used after the start. The first word always needs a capital letter.
asks: When do I use a big letter?

faq.q: What should I do when I see a full stop?
faq.a: When you see a full stop, you must stop talking completely. It is like taking a little breath before starting the next thought. You stop your voice right there.
asks: What sound do I make at the end?
How do I show a full stop?
Do I pause at a full stop?

faq.a: It means checking if the words you read make sense together. If the words sound silly, then the sentence does not make sense. You check if the story makes sense to you.
asks: How do I know if it makes sense?
What is the point of sense reading?
Does it have to sound right?

faq.q: If I read it wrong, what should I do?
faq.a: It is okay to read it wrong sometimes. Just stop, look back at the words, and try reading it again. You can always try again.

facts: Sentences always begin with a capital letter.
A full stop tells you to stop speaking.
Finger tracking helps you follow words while reading.
Reading for sense means checking if the story makes sense.

quiz.say: When reading, what should you do with your finger?

options.show: Point only at the first word.
options.say: Point only at the first word.

quiz.why: Pointing under each word helps your eyes follow the words correctly.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is easier, but moving your finger helps your brain track the words.
wrong.2: This is tempting because the first word is important, but you must point at every word.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it seems like pointing, but it does not help you follow the line of text.

quiz.say: The sentence 'The dog ran fast' is read. Does it make sense?
quiz.why: The words 'dog', 'ran', and 'fast' fit together to tell a clear story.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you are checking for sense, but these words form a clear, sensible idea.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you are trying to fix it, but the original words already make sense together.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might feel unsure, but you can check if the words tell a clear story.
